class="docs-prompt-preview" aria-label="Prompt preview" tabindex="0">You&#x27;re Claude Code, working in my repository.

Task
Add rewind to this project&#x27;s chat feature, the way Muse Code&#x27;s /rewind works: let the user pick an earlier user message, start a new branch that continues from the stored response before it (previous_response_id), put the picked message back in the composer as an editable draft, and keep the original thread unchanged and reachable. Store each turn&#x27;s response id so any branch can continue from any point.

Read this first
Meta&#x27;s docs page &quot;Rewind a conversation&quot; as Markdown: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/rewind.md
It&#x27;s the source of truth for request and response shapes. The same page for people: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/rewind

Setup
- Base URL: https://api.meta.ai/v1
- Auth: send Authorization: Bearer $MODEL_API_KEY, reading MODEL_API_KEY from the environment. Never hard-code, print or commit the key.
- Model: muse-spark-1.3-contributor (Contributor mode: Meta may use what you send to train future models; drop -contributor for Standard mode)
- Python: the OpenAI SDK (pip install openai) with base_url=&quot;https://api.meta.ai/v1&quot; and api_key=os.environ[&quot;MODEL_API_KEY&quot;] works, or plain requests.

Facts to get right
- POST https://api.meta.ai/v1/responses with previous_response_id continues a stored response (stored by default). Rewinding to message k continues from turn k-1&#x27;s response id, or from nothing for the first message.
- Send instructions on every call: they don&#x27;t carry over through previous_response_id.
- Rewind changes conversation history only. Whatever earlier turns did outside the chat stays done, so the UI should say so.
- The source branch keeps A, B, C; rewinding to B makes a child whose context is only A, with B as an unsent draft.
- Chaining can briefly fail right after a response is created (503, or 400 &quot;referenced response not found&quot;). Retry with backoff before giving up.
- Keep max_output_tokens at 400 or more: reasoning uses tokens too.

Starter code (Python)
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url=&quot;https://api.meta.ai/v1&quot;, api_key=os.environ[&quot;MODEL_API_KEY&quot;])
MODEL = &quot;muse-spark-1.3-contributor&quot;

def send(text, previous_id=None):
    chain = {&quot;previous_response_id&quot;: previous_id} if previous_id else {}
    r = client.responses.create(model=MODEL, input=text, instructions=&quot;Keep answers short.&quot;,
                                max_output_tokens=800, **chain)
    return r.id, r.output_text

thread = []  # (response_id, user_text) for every turn on the original branch
for text in [&quot;Suggest a rate-limiting approach.&quot;, &quot;Show the middleware.&quot;, &quot;Write a test.&quot;]:
    rid, _ = send(text, thread[-1][0] if thread else None)
    thread.append((rid, text))

k = 1  # rewind to B: continue from A&#x27;s response; B comes back as an editable draft
draft = thread[k][1]
branch_id, reply = send(draft + &quot; Use a Redis store.&quot;, thread[k - 1][0])
print(reply)

Done when
- A conversation A, B, C rewound to B gives a branch whose next request carries A&#x27;s response id as previous_response_id, with B in the composer.
- The original thread still shows A, B, C and can continue from C.
- The key comes from MODEL_API_KEY and never appears in code, logs or commits.</pre><div class="docs-prompt-foot"><span class="docs-prompt-count">3,188<!-- --> characters</span><button type="button" The child is also a normal retained session, so you can resume it later or rewind it again. Muse Code displays a divider when it moves your terminal into the branch:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">text</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="text" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line">• You're continuing from this point in a new conversation</span></code></pre></div></div><p class="docs-p">The earlier scrollback above that divider remains visible for orientation. Only the history before the selected input enters the child model&#x27;s context.</p><h2 id="workspace" class="docs-h docs-h2">Keep workspace changes separate<a class="docs-anchor" href="#workspace" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Rewind changes conversation history only. It does not restore, revert, or delete workspace files.</p><p class="docs-p">Any shell commands, subagents, workflows, approvals, or deliveries that still belong to the source session continue there. The action screen warns you when Muse Code detects active background work. The new branch does not receive those live task handles.</p><p class="docs-p">Review the working copy before you continue if the discarded conversation turns changed files. Restore code separately with your source-control tools when needed.</p><h2 id="availability" class="docs-h docs-h2">Read rewind availability<a class="docs-anchor" href="#availability" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">The picker labels each prior input:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Exact</strong>: Muse Code can recreate the branch and restore the selected input without known loss.</span></li><li><span><strong>Review required</strong>: Muse Code can create the branch, but part of the selected input is unavailable. The action screen describes the missing attachment or skill. Replace or remove any missing-content marker before you submit the restored draft.</span></li><li><span><strong>Blocked</strong>: Muse Code cannot prove that the branch would preserve valid history. Select the row to read the reason. Pressing <code class="docs-code-inline">Enter</code> does not continue from a blocked row.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">Some inputs do not appear as rewind targets. Rewind uses complete top-level turn boundaries. Mid-turn steering, pending queued input, local slash commands, and active turns are not separate rewind points.</p><p class="docs-p">Muse Code can also block a point when:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>The point is older than retained history.</span></li><li><span>The conversation contains Goal history that cannot cross the selected boundary.</span></li><li><span>A required attachment in the retained prefix is unavailable.</span></li><li><span>The retained tool history cannot be replayed safely.</span></li><li><span>The original input or plugin binding cannot be reconstructed safely.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">Older sessions can contain messages that predate rewind support. Muse Code identifies those messages in the picker or explains that the conversation has no supported rewind points.</p><h2 id="requirements" class="docs-h docs-h2">Know the session requirements<a class="docs-anchor" href="#requirements" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Rewind is available only in interactive terminal sessions with session logging enabled. It is unavailable in sessions started with <code class="docs-code-inline">muse --no-session-log</code>.</p><p class="docs-p">Open the picker with the <code class="docs-code-inline">/rewind</code> command, or with the double-<code class="docs-code-inline">Esc</code> gesture from an empty composer. def send(text, previous_id=None):
    chain = {&quot;previous_response_id&quot;: previous_id} if previous_id else {}
    r = client.responses.create(model=MODEL, input=text, instructions=&quot;Keep answers short.&quot;,
                                max_output_tokens=800, **chain)
    return r.id, r.output_text

thread = []  # (response_id, user_text) for every turn on the original branch
for text in [&quot;Suggest a rate-limiting approach.&quot;, &quot;Show the middleware.&quot;, &quot;Write a test.&quot;]:
    rid, _ = send(text, thread[-1][0] if thread else None)
    thread.append((rid, text))

k = 1  # rewind to B: continue from A&#x27;s response; B comes back as an editable draft
draft = thread[k][1]
branch_id, reply = send(draft + &quot; Use a Redis store.&quot;, thread[k - 1][0])
print(reply)

Done when
- A conversation A, B, C rewound to B gives a branch whose next request carries A&#x27;s response id as previous_response_id, with B in the composer.
- The original thread still shows A, B, C and can continue from C.
- The key comes from MODEL_API_KEY and never appears in code, logs or commits.</pre><div class="docs-prompt-foot"><span class="docs-prompt-count">3,188<!-- --> characters</span><button type="button" class="docs-btn docs-btn-primary docs-btn-sm"><svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span>Copy prompt</span></button></div></div></div><button type="button" class="docs-btn docs-btn-secondary" title="Copy this page as Markdown"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span>Copy page</span></button><a class="docs-btn docs-btn-secondary" href="https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/rewind" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M14 4h6v6 M20 4l-9 9 M18 14v4.5a1.5 1.5 0 0 1-1.5 1.5h-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 4 18.5v-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 5.5 6H10"></path></svg><span>View on dev.meta.ai</span><span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a><p class="docs-rail-note">Independent concept built on Meta&#x27;s Model API.
